P2.block:
Viability under perfect measurement has a complete theory: the viability kernel characterizes the states from which some feedback keeps the system within its constraints. When the state is observed only through an incomplete map, the sufficiency direction has a canonical answer — Veliov's output-feedback regulation condition, and the estimation-set reduction to perfect information. This paper supplies the complementary necessity theory: an obstruction calculus certifying when *no observation-based policy exists*. Four mechanisms are developed with complete proofs. (i) A finite-time exit certificate: under an Isaacs-type drift condition the disturbance forces constraint violation within a computable time, defeating every control of any information structure. (ii) A common-action obstruction: if the safe controls of the states compatible with the current information set intersect emptily, no observation-based policy is viable, though every compatible state is individually viable. (iii) A delayed-information obstruction with timing bound: information accurate but arriving after the enforced exit time cannot save the belief state. (iv) A certification limit: an exact observation-only certifier exists if and only if safe-set membership is constant on observation fibres. A fifth mechanism shows certainty-equivalence control under a biased observation emptying a nonempty perfect-information kernel. The calculus is positioned against barrier certificates and estimation tubes, and its consequences for monitoring design are drawn.

**Keywords:** viability theory; incomplete observation; output feedback; safety certification; differential inclusions; sustainability

The five mechanisms form a complete small taxonomy of information-theoretic failure. The exit certificate (Theorem 1) is the dynamic obstruction: it defeats all controls, so it needs no observation argument. The common-action obstruction (Theorem 3) is the static obstruction: it defeats all policies at a single information state. The delayed-information obstruction (Theorem 4) interpolates between them in time. The fibre criterion (Theorem 5) is the certification obstruction: it limits not policies but verdicts. The certainty-equivalence trap (Remark 1) limits policy classes. A governance failure of observation can be diagnosed by which certificate applies: if the exit certificate holds, no monitoring design helps — the dynamics are adverse under every control; if only the common-action obstruction holds, the remedy is a finer observation structure (an informative measurement distinguishing the incompatible states); if the delayed-information obstruction holds with a slack timing bound, the remedy is a shorter review interval or a faster indicator; if the fibre criterion fails, the remedy is per-floor observation rather than a better threshold on the aggregate.

A gated three-state model (stock, filtered deficit memory, deployed effort) responds to a delayed decline signal, and two effort laws of opposite sign structure are contrasted: a mobilising law whose gain grows with deployed effort, and a protective quota-tracking law whose gain restores. A complete cubic modulus condition is proved for the characteristic quasi-polynomial; a filter identity makes the cross term vanish identically, so positive roots occur in even pairs. For the mobilising channel, the two Hopf crossings are certified by interval Newton with outward rounding (τ− ∈ [3.6661490142739, 3.6661490142743] yr, τ+ ∈ [150.3584773101408, 150.3584773101421] yr); both are subcritical (ℓ1 = +5.75×10⁻⁵ and +3.55×10⁻⁴), and delay opens a phase-stabilised window in an undelayed-unstable system. ## Abstract
Classical delay studies place lags in the ecological dynamics of harvested populations; here the delay sits in the governance loop that converts observed stock decline into institutional response. A gated three-state model (stock, filtered deficit memory, deployed effort) contrasts two effort laws: a mobilising law whose gain grows with deployed effort, and a protective quota-tracking law whose gain restores. The imaginary-root condition reduces completely to a cubic modulus condition with a phase relation; a filter identity makes the cross term vanish, so positive roots occur with even multiplicity. For the mobilising channel, the two fundamental crossings of two positive Hopf-frequency families are interval-certified (τ− ∈ [3.6661490142739, 3.6661490142743] yr, τ+ ∈ [150.3584773101408, 150.3584773101421] yr); numerically evaluated positive first Lyapunov coefficients are consistent with subcritical bifurcations, and delay opens the fundamental phase-stabilised window. For the protective channel, a no-Hopf theorem holds at the calibrated quota-tracking point: loop gain peaks at 0.08011 < 1 and exponential stability holds for every delay. Under Euler-reviewed zero-order-hold sampling: annual protective review is stable (ρ = 0.9838), its instability threshold near 2.3 yr being a discretisation artefact — confirmed by the exact held-measurement update, which is stable at every tested review interval (maximum spectral radius 0.9967); annual mobilising review is unstable (ρ = 1.00055 Euler; 1.00035 exact) with a restabilising complex unit-circle crossing — the spectral signature of a Neimark–Sacker bifurcation, nonlinear conditions not verified — at 6.50 yr under the exact held-measurement update (the Euler-reported 47.536 yr crossing being a command-step artefact), the review interval being a local spectral design parameter, not a governance recommendation. Global numerics on the explored fundamental-delay range give a five-regime attractor topology whose lower boundary is a pair of nearby branch events, saddle-node classification provisional.

**Lemma (extra-loss threshold shift, conditional).** *In the constitutive model with an additional constant loss ($C>0$) or extra mortality ($M_x>0$), the effective threshold satisfies $\mathfrak s_{\rm eff}>\mathfrak s$, conditional on the modified positive equilibria existing and the loss lying below the relevant production maximum; larger losses eliminate the positive basin entirely.*

Two structural reasons explain the null. The long records needed to test the claim exist primarily for visible crises, and visibility is correlated with a fast non-institutional driver; and at any regeneration rate inside the instability window the predicted period is centuries, longer than any institution has held a fixed response rule. The visible-record pattern — long series repeatedly associated with climate variability, cohort effects, infrastructure changes, or emergency interventions — is consistent with a selection mechanism in which systems receive intensive monitoring after complex crises, but the retrospective search does not causally identify selection bias.

The case's positive result is a descriptive partition: **the exact data split the phenomenon into two events — the crash interpretation is formulation-dependent, and the non-recovery is unexplained in both formulations. The split is the positive result, not a new mechanism.**

This evaluation follows a preregistered retention rule: model structure is retained only when it improves early warning, out-of-sample prediction, or intervention selection. The test is applied to Northern cod in NAFO divisions 2J3KL. The primary predictand is the NCAM M-shift spawning-stock biomass (SSB) series of DFO (2016, Table A2) (the state-space assessment model of Cadigan, 2016) for 1983–2015, with the 2016 limit reference point (LRP) at the 1983–1989 mean SSB of 884.6 kt. Nested surplus-production models and two naive baselines issue fixed-window and rolling-origin forecasts. Catch enters as a coarse regime (240/120/5 kt) and as year-by-year landings (Schijns et al., 2021). No structural model has lower primary RMSE than last-value persistence. One-year rolling RMSE is 98 kt for persistence versus 115–196 kt for the surplus-production ladder under the coarse catch regime (115–206 kt across both catch treatments); year-by-year landings do not change the ranking (stock-flow RMSE 160 kt). Five-year RMSE is 265 kt versus 289–488 kt. The collapse window is missed by every model (RMSE 694–819 kt): a constant-productivity surplus model with a 1992 catch drop cannot produce the observed crash; neither an AR residual nor a one-year information delay reduces that error, and the delay raises it. On the recovery window the autonomous Allee fit has the lowest structural RMSE (90 kt) but is unidentified. The evaluation yields a negative certificate — a machine-verified non-retention finding, distinct from a statistical null result — rather than a forecast gain: the autonomous surplus-production model class is incompatible with the observed path; catch-regime stock-flow is not sufficient for collapse; and modules not identified on the training window increase error. The same retention rule holds on a second, unpooled specification (xteNCAM, 1954–2024, LRP 276 kt): persistence one-year RMSE 88 kt versus 120 kt for the autonomous Schaefer model. Capelin-informed productivity is not retained on the primary score. The series are not mixed.

**Keywords:** forecast evaluation; Northern cod; surplus production; model ablation; persistence; negative certificate

This evaluation follows a preregistered retention rule: additional model structure is retained only when it improves early warning, out-of-sample prediction, or intervention selection. The instrument is a scored model-ablation framework — a ladder of nested surplus-production models evaluated against two naive baselines. The ladder is output-only, stock-and-flow, residual, then delay and observation. A module is kept only if it improves a preregistered score. This paper is that empirical evaluation.

Intervention selection is scored rather than asserted: a governance module is kept only if it improves a declared protection-and-supply outcome, with the protocol frozen before any kernel was computed. The governed object is the one-step least-squares surplus-production map fitted on the 1983–2007 Northern cod (NAFO 2J3KL) spawning-stock series ($r = 0.2369$; $K = 5000$ kt, pinned at its optimization bound; residual SD 135.0 kt; residual lag-1 autocorrelation 0.65), scored on the declared catch-policy family — moratorium-level removals, flat caps, the DFO-2009 critical-zone rule, a cascade — against the 2016 limit reference point (884.6 kt) under persistent productivity floors, with stochastic, finite-duration, carrying-capacity, and bootstrap layers added as declared post-freeze analyses. (1) Under the informative 10th-percentile floor the moratorium and zero catch hold the entire safe set at every horizon, the largest robust constant catch is 57.6 kt ($g(K^*) - |e_{q10}| = 172.47 - 114.85$), and any rule harvesting at the boundary is less protective — the declared geometry of the rule's protective clause, stated as such. (2) The two harsher floors exceed the map's maximum surplus ($g_{\max} = 296$ kt yr⁻¹), so their emptiness holds for every policy, zero catch included: a vacuous robustness statement, qualified rather than read as a productivity finding. (3) The map is expansive at the LRP ($F' = 1.153$), the contraction form of certified conversion is inapplicable, and certified kernels are empty beyond five years; the expansion is the data-selected regime — $F' \ge 1$ at every carrying capacity at or above $2K^*$, and contraction below that level ($F' = 0.61$–$0.93$) is restored only where the informative certificates themselves collapse. (4) Stochastic viability on the empirical residual pool gives 20-year survival probabilities from the LRP of 0.87 (zero catch) to 0.58 (120 kt); the 57.6 kt boundary carries survival probability 0.77–0.88 by resampling scheme, and the 90% bootstrap interval of the constructive bound is $[0, 84.8]$ kt. (5) The data-preferred depensatory refit (SSE 7690 versus 12,772 kt²) leaves the constructive, selection, and expansion certificates intact and reverses only the vacuous 5th-percentile class. On this map, under these classes and this rule, the LRP is protected by good years rather than by catch management; the paper does not assert that conclusion for Northern cod productivity or for harvest-control rules in general.

E3.block: Index-well head forecasting is a recurring operational problem of groundwater management, and the literature offers an increasingly rich inventory of data-driven models. This evaluation follows a preregistered retention rule: model structure is retained only when it improves a preregistered out-of-sample score. The predictand is the calendar-year mean of daily-high elevation at the J-17 index well (TWDB 6837203), 1934–2023, in feet. Nested models issue fixed-window and rolling-origin forecasts; recharge and pumpage enter as candidate drivers. One-year rolling root-mean-square error (RMSE) is 13.23 ft for last-value persistence and 12.84 ft for a univariate AR(1), which is retained as an output-only model by a margin of 0.39 ft on 75 forecast origins. The causal stock-flow specification, which persists the most recent recharge and pumpage, has RMSE 14.70 ft and is rejected; a climatological stock-flow variant reaches 12.28 ft but collapses to an affine AR(1) under constant fluxes and is declined on class grounds. At five years, training-mean climatology (16.80 ft) beats persistence (21.11 ft): five-year forecasts on this basin are climatology. Given realized future recharge and pumpage, the same map reaches 7.55 ft — a rent of nearly half the persistence error that no signal available at the annual origin recovers. Climate-informed recharge forecasts (lagged Niño 3.4, lagged precipitation) lie within 0.13 ft of AR(1) at one year and are worse than persistence at five years; none is retained. Contemporaneous Comal Springs discharge tracks J-17 (r = 0.986) but is a measured service of the same state, not an independent information source.

M1 is retained by the point-RMSE rule. The margin is 0.39 ft on n = 75 and is not a significance claim: it records a slightly mean-reverting head series, not a confirmation of stock-flow structure. M2m is listed by the same rule and then declined on class grounds fixed in the protocol (constant fluxes reduce it to AR(1)); its numerical advantage does not constitute additional structure. No stock-flow, residual, or delay module is retained.
